candidates.name: llm-surge-2
candidates.source:
NAME = "surge-2"

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    # Anticipatory: value the current push AND the push the next seed will make.
    # On the convex shoulder of an S-curve (H3 quadratic logit, H5 sqrt-probit)
    # slope(a+1) > slope(a), so seeds that park out-neighbours one step below
    # the steep region are worth more than hub's one-step marginal suggests.
    P0, P1, P2 = prob(f.a), prob(f.a + 1), prob(f.a + 2)
    D = np.where(f.eligible, P1 - P0, 0.0)      # value of pushing now
    Dn = np.where(f.eligible, P2 - P1, 0.0)     # value of the *next* push
    return D @ graph.adjT + 0.8 * (Dn @ graph.adjT) + f.eligible * (1.0 - P0)

candidates.name: llm-cascade-2
candidates.source:
NAME = "cascade-2"

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    # Two-step cascade value. A seed u can activate out-neighbour v this round
    # (D_v), and if v activates (prob ~ P1_v) it becomes an active in-neighbour
    # NEXT round and spreads further: that future spreading power is
    # S_v = sum over v's out-neighbours of the marginal there. Hub scores an
    # activated node as a flat 1; this prices it at its downstream reach --
    # a real gain under the noisy laws (H1/H2) where mid-range probabilities
    # make second hops frequent, and under any law on hub-heavy graphs.
    P0, P1 = prob(f.a), prob(f.a + 1)
    D = np.where(f.eligible, P1 - P0, 0.0)
    S = D @ graph.adjT                          # per-node one-round spreading value
    F = D + np.where(f.eligible, P1, 0.0) * S   # value of node v being active
    return F @ graph.adjT + f.eligible * (1.0 - P0)

candidates.name: llm-lookahead-2
candidates.source:
NAME = "lookahead-2"

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    # Hub only values the *first* marginal (P1 - P0). Under threshold laws whose
    # shoulder sits at a ~ 2, the node receiving its 2nd active in-neighbour is
    # worth far more than the node receiving its 1st. Value both differences:
    # trade a bit of spread now for leaving nodes one step from activation.
    P0 = prob(f.a)
    P1 = prob(f.a + 1)
    P2 = prob(f.a + 2)
    D1 = np.where(f.eligible, P1 - P0, 0.0)
    D2 = np.where(f.eligible, P2 - P1, 0.0)
    D = D1 + 0.6 * D2
    gain = D @ graph.adjT + f.eligible * (1.0 - P0)
    return gain + 1e-3 * f.eligible

candidates.name: llm-two-wave
candidates.source:
NAME = "two-wave"

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    # Second-order hub: a seed u pushes its out-neighbours v over the line
    # (w.p. P1-P0); each newly activated v in turn pushes *its* out-neighbours
    # w one step up (w.p. P2-P1). Hub drops this second wave entirely; on the
    # quadratic/logistic laws the second difference is the big one.
    P0 = prob(f.a)
    P1 = prob(f.a + 1)
    P2 = prob(f.a + 2)
    D1 = np.where(f.eligible, P1 - P0, 0.0)
    D2 = np.where(f.eligible, P2 - P1, 0.0)
    # R[v] = expected push that an activated v gives to its out-neighbours
    R = D2 @ graph.adjT
    second = (D1 * R) @ graph.adjT
    gain = D1 @ graph.adjT + 0.5 * second + f.eligible * (1.0 - P0)
    return gain + 1e-3 * f.eligible

candidates.name: llm-reservoir-3
candidates.source:
NAME = "reservoir-3"

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    # Inactive nodes persist between rounds, so a seed that leaves many targets
    # just below threshold builds a reservoir that pays out over later rounds.
    # Sum the geometrically discounted sequence of marginals (D1, D2, D3):
    # this ranks seeds by total future activation potential, not just the
    # one-round gain, and keeps a non-zero own-activation reach term.
    P0 = prob(f.a)
    P1 = prob(f.a + 1)
    P2 = prob(f.a + 2)
    P3 = prob(f.a + 3)
    D1 = np.where(f.eligible, P1 - P0, 0.0)
    D2 = np.where(f.eligible, P2 - P1, 0.0)
    D3 = np.where(f.eligible, P3 - P2, 0.0)
    D = D1 + 0.7 * D2 + 0.4 * D3
    gain = D @ graph.adjT + 0.5 * f.eligible * (1.0 - P0)
    return gain + 1e-3 * f.eligible

candidates.source:
NAME = "primer-2"

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    P0, P1, P2 = prob(f.a), prob(f.a + 1), prob(f.a + 2)
    imm = P1 - P0                                  # immediate marginal of each target
    deep = P1 < 0.05                               # still ~impossible even with +1 in-neighbour
    primer = np.where(deep, P2, 0.0)               # one further push (next round) fires it
    per = imm + 0.85 * primer                      # discount for the one-round delay
    return per @ graph.adjT + f.eligible * (1.0 - P0)

candidates.source:
NAME = "pipeline-2"

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    P0, P1 = prob(f.a), prob(f.a + 1)
    imm = P1 - P0
    extra = P1 @ graph.adj                    # expected added active in-neighbours next round
    nxt = prob(f.a + 1 + extra) - P1          # marginal those additions unlock next round
    second = nxt @ graph.adjT                 # value, per target v, of activating v now
    return (imm + 0.75 * second) @ graph.adjT + f.eligible * (1.0 - P0)

candidates.source:
NAME = "prob-gate-2"

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    P0, P1, P2 = prob(f.a), prob(f.a + 1), prob(f.a + 2)
    comp = (f.eligible & (f.a == 1)).astype(float) * P1   # gate completion, prob-weighted
    prog = (f.eligible & (f.a < 1)).astype(float) * P2    # priming, prob-weighted
    extra = comp @ graph.adj                              # completed nodes spread next round
    nxt = prob(f.a + 1 + extra) - P1
    second = nxt @ graph.adjT
    return (comp + 0.4 * prog) @ graph.adjT + 0.7 * second + 1e-3 * f.eligible

candidates.name: llm-bank-2
candidates.source:
NAME = "bank-2"

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    # hub + a discounted "banking" term: seeding u pushes each out-neighbour v from
    # a_v to a_v+1; the extra marginal (a_v+1 -> a_v+2) is the value a later seed
    # can harvest. hub ignores that setting up near-gates now has option value
    # across rounds; bank-2 pays for it.
    P0 = prob(f.a)
    P1 = prob(f.a + 1)
    P2 = prob(f.a + 2)
    d1 = np.where(f.eligible, P1 - P0, 0.0)   # immediate marginal at each target
    d2 = np.where(f.eligible, P2 - P1, 0.0)   # marginal left after our +1 (banked)
    base = d1 @ graph.adjT + f.eligible * (1.0 - P0)
    bank = d2 @ graph.adjT
    return base + 0.25 * bank + 1e-3 * f.eligible

candidates.name: llm-lowdeg-first
candidates.source:
NAME = "lowdeg-first"

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    # Under capped / indegree-normalised laws the first active in-neighbour of a
    # low-indeg target is worth far more than one more in-neighbour of a dense-in
    # node. hub credits every out-neighbour equally; here each target's marginal
    # is reweighted by 1/log(indeg), so seeds pointing at cheap gates rise and
    # seeds dumping influence into dense-in sinks fall.
    P0 = prob(f.a)
    P1 = prob(f.a + 1)
    d = np.where(f.eligible, P1 - P0, 0.0)
    w = 1.0 / np.log1p(f.indeg + 1.0)              # low-indeg targets convert +1 into activation
    w = w * (w.size / max(w.sum(), 1e-9))          # keep the scale of hub's spread term
    return (d * w) @ graph.adjT + f.eligible * (1.0 - P0) + 1e-3 * f.eligible

candidates.name: llm-sat-avoid
candidates.source:
NAME = "sat-avoid"

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    # hub counts the full marginal d_v for every out-neighbour, even targets that
    # would have activated anyway this round; those activations are not really
    # attributable to the seed and make the greedy chase already-lost nodes.
    # Credit only the "surprise" part: d scaled by (1 - P1), i.e. flips of nodes
    # that were still unlikely without the extra in-neighbour.
    P0 = prob(f.a)
    P1 = prob(f.a + 1)
    d = np.where(f.eligible, P1 - P0, 0.0)
    spread = d @ graph.adjT
    waste = (d * P1) @ graph.adjT                  # part of spread into targets already near-activated
    return spread + f.eligible * (1.0 - P0) - 0.5 * waste + 1e-3 * f.eligible

candidates.name: llm-relay-2
candidates.source:
NAME = "relay-2"

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    # one fresh exposure: generic marginal, valid for every hypothesis
    d1 = prob(np.ones_like(f.a)) - prob(np.zeros_like(f.a))     # (M, n), per target node
    D = np.where(f.eligible, prob(f.a + 1) - prob(f.a), 0.0)    # law-aware marginal right now
    p1 = np.where(f.eligible, 1.0 - prob(f.a), 0.0)             # the seed itself activates
    # spread capacity: expected activations a node causes if it fires next round
    cap = d1 @ graph.adjT                                        # (M, n)
    relay = d1 * cap                                             # value of triggering each node once more
    first = D @ graph.adjT + p1
    return first + 0.5 * (relay @ graph.adjT) + 1e-3 * f.eligible

candidates.name: llm-gate-auto
candidates.source:
NAME = "gate-auto"

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    D = prob(f.a + 1) - prob(f.a)                        # marginal of the next exposure
    comp = f.eligible * D * (1.0 - prob(f.a))            # decisive final push (works for any gate g)
    prog = f.eligible * D * np.exp(-f.a)                 # depth-decayed progress at any level
    reach = f.eligible * (1.0 - prob(f.a))               # non-zero tie bar, as hub keeps
    return (comp + 0.3 * prog) @ graph.adjT + 0.1 * D @ graph.adjT + 1e-3 * reach

candidates.name: llm-densify
candidates.source:
NAME = "densify"

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    warm = (f.E > 0).astype(float)                       # nodes already carrying memory
    hot = warm * np.minimum(f.a, 3.0)                    # partway nodes: extra exposure compounds
    dens = (warm + 2.0 * hot) @ graph.adjT               # memory-rich reach per candidate
    D = np.where(f.eligible, prob(f.a + 1) - prob(f.a), 0.0)
    return f.eligible * 0.5 * dens + D @ graph.adjT + 1e-3 * f.eligible

candidates.name: llm-fresh-dose-1
candidates.source:
NAME = "fresh-dose-1"

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    # Under power-law fatigue the marginal value of an exposure dose decays
    # sharply with cumulative exposure already banked (sharper than 1/E).
    # Price each target's dose with a still-sharper freshness weight, so the
    # planner stops wasting exposures on saturated hubs and banks doses on
    # fresh targets instead -- something prime (flat exposure credit) misses.
    P0, P1 = prob(f.a), prob(f.a + 1)
    marg = np.where(f.eligible, P1 - P0, 0.0)      # immediate activation marginal
    fresh = np.where(f.eligible, 1.0 / (1.0 + f.E) ** 2, 0.0)
    # spread now always counts; a dose to a fresh target is worth extra later,
    # a dose to a near-saturated target is worth less than none at all.
    X = marg * (1.0 + fresh) - 0.25 * marg * (1.0 - fresh)
    return X @ graph.adjT + f.eligible * (1.0 - P0) + 1e-3 * f.eligible

candidates.name: llm-combo-2
candidates.source:
NAME = "combo-2"

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    # Relative novelty gates on current stimulation a vs cumulative k*E, so
    # single doses are nearly worthless but a burst of two simultaneous
    # actives on a target lands it past the gate. Value each candidate not
    # only by its own marginal push, but by the *second* stimulation it sets
    # up on a target another seed is likely to also reach (degree-based
    # likelihood), using prob(f.a+2) for the anticipated bonus.
    P0, P1, P2 = prob(f.a), prob(f.a + 1), prob(f.a + 2)
    marg = np.where(f.eligible, P1 - P0, 0.0)
    second = np.where(f.eligible, P2 - P1, 0.0)
    partner = f.indeg / (f.indeg.max() + 1.0)      # chance another seed hits it
    X = (marg + 0.5 * second * partner)
    return X @ graph.adjT + f.eligible * (1.0 - P0) + 1e-3 * f.eligible

candidates.name: llm-slot-eff-2
candidates.source:
NAME = "slot-eff-2"

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    # Exponential fatigue charges per exposure *round*, so every round a
    # target is exposed without activating permanently lowers its hazard.
    # Exposure slots must be spent only where the push actually flips the
    # node: weight each target's marginal activation by its post-push
    # activation probability P1, concentrating doses on near-certain kills
    # and refusing to tease gates that are still far away.
    P0, P1 = prob(f.a), prob(f.a + 1)
    marg = np.where(f.eligible, P1 - P0, 0.0)
    X = marg * P1 + 0.05 * np.where(f.eligible, P1, 0.0) * (marg <= 0.0)
    return X @ graph.adjT + f.eligible * (1.0 - P0) + 1e-3 * f.eligible
